blocks.source: Vol IV, Safety Enforcement, § The Per-Tick Gatekeeper
blocks.md: Every physical AI system ends in the same act. A command leaves software, becomes current in a motor winding, and puts momentum into a world that does not roll back. Safety enforcement is the runtime mechanism that decides, one control tick at a time, whether the next command may cross that causal boundary. Checking a plan once before it runs does not settle the question, because admission judges the plan against the state the planner predicted, and the machine then executes it against the state it actually reaches.

questions.q: The section **The Per-Tick Gatekeeper** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Speed and separation monitoring keeps a protective separation distance (the person's travel, the robot's reaction and stopping travel, intrusion distance, and position uncertainties) between a moving arm and a person as a certified function.

The enforcement record joins a signed enforcement contract (tracking bound, barrier coefficients, deadlines, effort-error bounds, routing) to a per-tick admitted command with its margin, detector, and rung.

A least-change projection passes a safe proposal untouched and projects a violating one onto the barrier boundary, keeping learned competence, while a structurally invalid proposal is vetoed rather than corrected.
Available deceleration is net of gravity and bias in the worst direction, and integrator unwinding and saturation spend it before the stop begins.
